papers.title: Recovering Irreducible Three-Body Interactions with Lagrangian Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Lagrangian Neural Networks (LNNs) learn mechanical systems from trajectory data by parameterizing a scalar Lagrangian and deriving the dynamics through the Euler-Lagrange equations, biasing the model toward motion that respects the variational structure of mechanics. The interactions studied so far have been pairwise-additive, leaving open whether LNNs can recover an irreducible many-body interaction from motion alone. We address this using the Axilrod-Teller triple-dipole interaction, the leading three-body dispersion term, whose dependence on the collective geometry of three particles cannot be represented by any sum of pairwise terms. We prescribe the kinetic energy exactly and learn only the potential, as a function of interparticle distances and angles. Combined with a signal-aware sampling strategy that concentrates training data where the three-body signal is strongest while preserving broad coverage of configuration space, this recovers the interaction from accelerations alone. The learned potential reproduces the radial scaling, angular dependence, and characteristic sign reversal of the Axilrod-Teller interaction, and generates stable trajectories. Embedding it within a pairwise Lennard-Jones potential lets us examine its observability: the three-body term is recovered once its dynamical signature exceeds the residual modeling error, which it does cleanly at amplified coupling but not at the coupling of a real noble gas, bracketing the transition between the two. Finally, symbolic regression on the trained potential, with no assumed functional form, returns the Axilrod-Teller expression with angular numerator, radial law, and coupling constant intact. An LNN with domain-specific structure can thus recover an irreducible three-body interaction from trajectories as a closed-form law, pointing toward learning interaction laws whose structure is not known a priori.

papers.title: Correlated Pair Creation with Positive- and Negative-Frequency Oscillators in a Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulator
papers.abstract: Spin-dependent forces enable independent control over the effective frequencies of bosonic motional modes and their coupling strengths to spins in trapped-ion spin-boson quantum simulators. We show that the relative signs of these effective frequencies provide an important programmable resource for engineering distinct multimode dynamics. Focusing on a two-mode quantum Rabi model, changing the frequencies of the two modes from the same sign to opposite signs reorganizes the resonance structure of the spin-mediated bosonic interaction, converting the dominant resonant process from excitation exchange to correlated pair creation. In the dispersive regime, the resulting effective interaction realizes a two-mode parametric amplifier with stable oscillatory, critical, and exponentially amplifying regimes separated by a spin-dependent instability threshold. Across these regimes, the dynamics generate collective-quadrature squeezing and bipartite motional entanglement. Preparing the spin in a coherent superposition further allows different spin components to experience distinct stability regimes, generating tripartite spin-boson entanglement, while spin postselection can coherently combine the conditional bosonic branches to generate non-Gaussian entangled bosonic states. Finally, we outline an implementation using parameters within reach of current trapped-ion platforms.

papers.title: Superconducting-antiqubit simulation enables optimal phase estimation via unitary inversion
papers.abstract: A positron is equivalent to an electron traveling backward through time. Casting transmon superconducting qubits as akin to electrons, we simulate a positron with a transmon subject to particular resonant and off-resonant drives. We call positron-like transmons "antiqubits." An antiqubit's effective gyromagnetic ratio equals the negative of a qubit's. This fact enables us to time-invert a unitary implemented on a transmon by its environment. We apply this platform-specific unitary inversion, with qubit--antiqubit entanglement, to achieve a quantum advantage in phase estimation: consider measuring the strength of a field that points in an unknown direction. An entangled qubit--antiqubit sensor offers the greatest possible sensitivity (amount of Fisher information), per qubit, per application of the field. We prove this result theoretically and observe it experimentally. This work shows how antimatter, whether real or simulated, can enable platform-specific unitary inversion and benefit quantum information processing.

papers.title: Quantum dynamics of an ion in an RF quadrupole trap with weak octupolar anharmonicity
papers.abstract: We investigate the quantum dynamics of a single ion confined in a radio-frequency (RF) Paul trap in the presence of weak octupole-induced anharmonicity, as can occur in realistic ion-trap potential. The explicitly time-dependent quadrupole potential is treated in a reference-oscillator Fock basis, allowing the effects of the RF drive and the quartic correction to be resolved directly at the level of motional-state couplings. While the quadratic RF interaction generates $\Delta n=\pm2$ transitions and Gaussian squeezing, the quartic contribution opens additional $\Delta n=\pm4$ coupling pathways. Starting from the reference-oscillator vacuum, we show that the octupole interaction broadens the even-parity Fock-state distribution and enhances the phonon-number fluctuations more strongly than the mean occupation. At the same time, the RF-induced sub-vacuum quadrature squeezing remains robust, although its magnitude and orientation are modified by the quartic interaction. The number statistics and quadrature fluctuations therefore respond differently to the same nonlinear perturbation, reflecting the distinct roles of Fock-space redistribution and phase coherence. The resulting dynamics provide a quantum-mechanical characterization of weak octupole corrections beyond the ideal quadrupole approximation and clarify how realistic anharmonicities modify nonclassical trapped-ion motion. Importantly, the motional nonclassicality remains robust against the weak octupole perturbation, as evidenced by persistent sub-vacuum quadrature squeezing and Klyshko-inequality violation. These results characterize how realistic anharmonic corrections reshape trapped-ion motion beyond the ideal quadrupole approximation.

papers.title: Optical atomic clocks on all-optical atom chips
papers.abstract: The feasibility and potential performance of optical clocks based on all-optical atom chips using neutral strontium atoms have been investigated. The key benefits of all-optical atom chips are their ability to trap alkali-earth atoms, and how easily these atoms can be manipulated and examined. The planar configuration of the chip enables ring photonic resonators to be incorporated into its structure, making it a promising candidate for active optical atomic clocks. Using the 'magic wavelengths' of the trapping optical fields (813 nm and 390 nm for strontium atoms) minimises frequency shifts in the intercombination clock transition caused by variations in optical field intensity. However, this frequency shift can be compensated for using optical AC Stark shifts, which are generated by the trapping optical fields and have frequencies below the 'magic frequencies'. Furthermore, it has been demonstrated that atom chip clocks can operate using solely repulsive, blue-detuned evanescent light fields when the attraction of the trapped atoms towards the photonic waveguide is realised through van der Waals forces alone. According to estimates, this could result in the short-term fractional frequency stability of the strontium atom-chip optical clocks being limited to ~10^{-16} per second, with an accuracy of about 5 x 10^{-15} for fractional intensity stability in the trapping light fields of 0.001.

papers.title: Optimal Calibration-Free Observable for the Nucleon-Coupling Ratio in a Dual-Alkali Comagnetometer for Dark Matter Searches
papers.abstract: A dual-alkali single-cell $^{87}$Rb-$^{39}$K-$^{3}$He comagnetometer can read an axion-like dark matter signal through two optical rotation channels, encoding the ratio $\mathcal{R}=\xi_n/\xi_p$ of the field's neutron and proton spin couplings in their relative response. The inter-species phase difference $\Delta\varphi$ has been proposed as a calibration-free readout that is sensitive to $\mathcal{R}$. Treating the extraction of $\mathcal{R}$ as a statistical estimation problem, we show that the estimate of $\mathcal{R}$ depends on the two channels only through their complex ratio, which splits into $\Delta\varphi$ and an amplitude ratio, of which only $\Delta\varphi$ is insensitive to the relative gain and hence calibration free. For our choice of comagnetometer parameters, above $\sim\!100$ Hz the phase difference alone captures most of the coupling-ratio information. At lower frequencies $\Delta\varphi$ is no longer near-sufficient. Below $\sim\!40$ Hz, the amplitude ratio would improve the precision on $\mathcal{R}$ by a factor of $\gtrsim2$. Recovering that information, however, requires the relative gain to be known sufficiently accurately, so $\Delta\varphi$ remains the robust observable even where it is not the most informative one.

papers.title: CDW-EIS calculations of atomic ionization by bare ions and antiprotons
papers.abstract: We present \textit{ab initio} calculations of atomic ionization by bare ions and antiprotons within the continuum distorted-wave eikonal initial-state (CDW-EIS) model. The dataset covers atomic targets from H to Kr, impacted by bare ions over a broad range of projectile charges and by antiprotons. Particular attention is given to elements in periods 3 and 4 of the periodic table, which are relevant to pigment analysis and technologically important materials. The resulting subshell-resolved total ionization cross sections are made openly available through an online repository covering a broad range of projectile--target systems, occupied initial subshells, and projectile velocities. We analyze systematic trends in the cross sections, including their dependence on projectile charge and velocity, binding-energy scaling, and charge-sign effects in proton and antiproton impact. To extend the practical coverage of the database, we also develop a neural-network surrogate, CDWEIS-NN, trained on the subset of the database with projectile charge $|Z_\mathrm{P}|\leq 8$. The network interpolates the CDW-EIS results to additional projectile--target systems and impact energies, reproducing both held-out CDW-EIS calculations and the experimental benchmarks considered in this work with satisfactory accuracy.
